objective: Strengthen BUKLOD mandatory native update enforcement across all routes with an actionable Filipino update screen, bounded foreground version policy refresh, and faster safe OTA adoption checks; preserve the release gate before enabling a mass outdated APK cutoff.
productionBaselineEvidence: Supabase production app_runtime_config production minimum_supported_version=1.0.0, recommended_version=1.0.0, maintenance_mode=false. 132 active Android installation records in trailing 30 days all reported 1.3.4/runtime 1.3.2; registry reports native_build=NULL and cannot distinguish some older build 26 from v28. GitHub main c8f55f91fb0d1e792385a7dc449a6ef1938ef42c; production OTA release ID/new APK verification not available. Do not raise cutoff before verified compatible production update and recovery access.
chosenApproach: Centralized version gate at root Stack for authenticated native traffic while retaining original route aliases, actionable Play Store/browser update and check-again, web version exempt from native APK cutoff, throttled foreground config refresh, 1-hour foreground Expo OTA check and manual restart to protect calls/PTT.
selectionRationale: Keeps server as the only cutoff authority; avoids disabling users until verified release and update path is available; closes route/deeplink bypass; no native SDK change or Supabase migration.
alternativeApproaches: Immediately raise production minimum version to 1.3.4 before verifying OTA and store availability: rejected due to lockout risk and shared version string across native build 26 and 28.
Install new native build remotely without user action: impossible with OTA; binary update needs Play Store or sideload.
Introduce native build-level cutoff via unverified constants: rejected, telemetry reports no reliable native build; requires later native release/verified build metadata.
Gate across root with helpful update path and keep minimum server cutoff unchanged until verified RC: selected.
preserveBehaviors: Authenticated users can use app normally until server policy explicitly marks version obsolete
